what: Re-run of the 2026-09-29 LM-load memory probes, this time on a verified-empty board.
why: The 09-29 probes were run WITHOUT an occupancy check (no `whoelse` between 09-28T15:55Z and 09-30T19:54Z). Their conclusion -- 'memory IS binding at load' -- was sent to the LM track and partly reopened INT8 there.
board: jetson-lpcv-03, L4T R36.4.7, nvpmodel 0 (15 W), rebooted ~2026-10-01 10:37
occupancy: verified before and after every run: 0 users, 0 non-mine processes >1% CPU, no foreign containers, no /dev/nvidia* clients
reclaim: none -- no drop_file_cache.py, unlike the 09-29 probes

findings.lm_only_does_not_fail_on_an_empty_board: 7 successes at MemFree 1508-4034 MB; 1 failure at 1084 MB. The 09-29 failures at 3863-4641 MB do not replicate.
findings.co_resident_config_loads: trt_then_lm and lm_then_trt BOTH succeed, at 1258 and 1470 MB free. This is the configuration the end-to-end sustained run needs.
findings.memavailable_was_not_a_hardware_ceiling: 09-29 capped at 5304 MB and I wrote 'the board physically cannot give much more than ~5 GB free'. Empty, it is 6692-6732 MB -- ~1.4 GB higher.
findings.the_4_2_gb_peak_was_inferred_not_measure: Measured peak torch device allocation is 0.98 GB every run, and host consumption is ~1.1-1.6 GB of MemFree. The '~4.2 GB peak' figure was arithmetic over an assumed 250k materialisation, never a measurement.
findings.page_cache_is_not_the_obstacle: lm_only succeeds with Cached at 3791-4255 MB and MemFree at 1508-2014 MB, so the load does not require page cache to be evicted first.

status: 'memory IS binding at load' is NOT ESTABLISHED and is withdrawn. The load is tight (MemFree falls to 132-699 MB) and can fail near ~1.1 GB free, but it is not the ceiling claimed, and the evidence for the claim was uncontrolled.
